## PR Description

## What

Ports the awf `factory-teammate.yml` «Apply the review verdict (review runs only)» step to dmtools-agents as CommonJS agent code — the keystone block of the sh→JS factory migration (policy: all factory domain logic → js/factory/, awf becomes thin plumbing; sh + A/B harness stay intact in awf until the final rewire PR).

- `js/factory/review_verdict.js` — the orchestration: fallback-source fetches (pack `loop/verdict.sh` wins, legacy `setup/review-verdict.sh` fallback), machineAuthor resolution, eval-safe key=value contract parse, label transitions, escalation comment + GraphQL review-threads query, CI-green poll gate (≤10 min), loud no-verdict path (gh-305).
- `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js` — JSRunner entry (`dmtools run`), resolveParams customParams>env>defaults, exit-1 on the loud no-verdict path.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — TDD suite, **30/30 green**.
- `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — jq-aware gh-stub parity harness: runs the REAL sh spec (byte-verbatim snapshot of awf scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ #34) and the JS side through the SAME stub world, byte-compares gh_calls.log argv, graphql payload, posted comment bytes, rc, warn lines.

## Layer plan

1. **Layer 1 — APPROVE path** (verdict extraction → CI poll → pr_approved latch): target 100% byte parity.
2. **Layer 2 — CHANGES/rework rc semantics** (re-label agent:rework under cap, round-label strip).
3. **Layer 3 — escalation / needs-human / poll-deadline loops** (cap → needs-human + threads comment, pending-forever deadline invariants).

## Current counts (updated as layers go green)

- unit: 30/30
- parity: RUNNING — counts will be updated in this body per layer (scenario classes: deterministic 7 + randomized 100).

## Harness notes (this session)

- stub rollup branch: poll-counter + CHECKS_STATE flip piped through the caller's --jq (the old mergeStateStatus case never matched the spec's argv → approve scenarios polled a real 600 s deadline).
- runSh is exec-wrapped so the 20 s SIGKILL wall kills the poll loop itself (no orphaned busy-loops); JS side gets a fake clock (+30 s/call) via the new deps.clock/deps.sleepMs seam in the entry.
- node_testRunner: scm.js preload fixed to mirror testRunner.js (makeRequire for machineNotice).

Merge gate per policy: full parity + the #889 canary leg, then the rewire PR.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Apply the review verdict (review runs only)) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block stays on the workflow step.
  if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    echo "::warning::SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN not set — verdict labels would not trigger workflows; skipping (a maintainer must label manually)"
    exit 0
  fi
  repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
  labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --json labels \
    --jq '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")' 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
  find_linked_pr() {
    gh pr list --repo "$repo" --state open \
      --json number,body,headRefName --jq '
      [.[] | select(
          ((.body // "") | test("(?i)\\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\\s+#'"$NUMBER"'\\b"))
          or (.headRefName | test("^'"$NUMBER"'[-_.]"))
          or (.headRefName | test("(^|[-_./])gh-0*'"$NUMBER"'$")))
        | .number] | first // empty'
  }
  pr="$(find_linked_pr)"
  # Verdict fallback sources beyond the run output (gh-305): what
  # the leg itself wrote on the PR (comments + review bodies) and
  # on the issue. A failed fetch leaves the file absent — the
  # parser's diagnosis reports it as `missing`, never a hard stop.
  verdict_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
  trap 'rm -rf "$verdict_dir"' EXIT
  pr_comments_json="${verdict_dir}/pr_comments.json"
  issue_comments_json="${verdict_dir}/issue_comments.json"
  if [ -n "$pr" ]; then
    gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$repo" --json comments,reviews \
      --jq '[(.comments // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}] + [(.reviews // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}]' \
      > "$pr_comments_json" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$pr_comments_json"
  fi
  gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --json comments \
    --jq '[(.comments // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}]' \
    > "$issue_comments_json" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$issue_comments_json"
  # machineAuthor resolution order #2 (js/common/machineAuthor.js):
  # deployments that set the per-repo .dmtools/config.js knob but
  # not the workflow input. Best-effort — empty on miss (then only
  # *[bot] comment authors are trusted).
  if [ -z "${MACHINE_AUTHOR:-}" ] && [ -r .dmtools/config.js ]; then
    MACHINE_AUTHOR="$(sed -nE 's/.*machineAuthor["'\'']?[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*["'\'']([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)["'\''].*/\1/p' .dmtools/config.js | head -1)"
  fi
  # Wave 2 (owner 2026-10-01): the verdict logic versions WITH the
  # reviewed pack — the unpacked pack's loop/verdict.sh WINS; the
  # legacy delegation `bash factory-agents/setup/review-verdict.sh decide`
  # remains the fallback for old pins. The pack cache
  # (~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/) is guaranteed populated
  # here: the agent run above resolved the review pack parent.
  VERDICT_SH="${FACTORY_ROOT}/setup/review-verdict.sh"
  review_agent="$(basename "${CONFIG}" .json)"
  pack_verdict="$(ls -1 "${HOME}"/.dmtools/packs/"${review_agent}"-*/loop/verdict.sh 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1 || true)"
  if [ -n "${pack_verdict}" ]; then
    VERDICT_SH="${pack_verdict}"
    echo "→ verdict logic: pack ${VERDICT_SH}"
  else
    echo "→ verdict logic: legacy tree ${VERDICT_SH} (no ${review_agent} pack loop/verdict.sh unpacked)"
  fi
  # Decision (pure logic, eval-safe key=value output): decision,
  # source, override, blocking_markers, rounds_done, next_round,
  # escalate, round_labels, diagnosis.
  eval "$(MAX_ROUNDS="${MAX_ROUNDS}" \
    PR_REVIEW_JSON="outputs/pr_review.json" \
    PR_REVIEW_JSON_ALT="outputs/gh-${NUMBER}/pr_review.json" \
    RUN_OUTPUT="${RUN_OUTPUT}" \
    PR_COMMENTS_JSON="${pr_comments_json}" \
    ISSUE_COMMENTS_JSON="${issue_comments_json}" \
    MACHINE_AUTHOR="${MACHINE_AUTHOR:-}" \
    ISSUE_LABELS="${labels}" \
    bash "${VERDICT_SH}" decide)"
  decision="${decision:-unknown}"
  escalate="${escalate:-false}"
  rounds_done="${rounds_done:-0}"
  next_round="${next_round:-0}"
  echo "→ review decision: ${decision} (source=${source:-none}, override=${override:-false}, rounds_done=${rounds_done})"
  strip_round_labels() {
    for lbl in ${round_labels:-}; do
      gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "$lbl" || true
    done
  }
  # bash -e: a missing label would abort the verdict transition —
  # create-or-update first (--force is an idempotent no-op).
  ensure_label() {
    gh label create "$1" --repo "$repo" --color "$2" --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  }
  if [ "$decision" = "rework" ]; then
    if [ "$escalate" = "true" ]; then
      strip_round_labels
      ensure_label "needs-human" "B60205"
      gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --add-label "needs-human"
      thread_summary=""
      if [ -n "$pr" ]; then
        owner="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY%%/*}"
        name="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}"
        threads_json="$(mktemp)"
        if gh api graphql \
          -f query='query($owner:String!,$name:String!,$number:Int!){repository(owner:$owner,name:$name){pullRequest(number:$number){reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{isResolved path line comments(first:1){nodes{body author{login}}}}}}}}' \
          -f owner="$owner" -f name="$name" -F number="$pr" \
          > "$threads_json"; then
          thread_summary="$(bash "${VERDICT_SH}" threads "$threads_json")"
        else
          echo "::warning::reviewThreads fetch failed — the findings live in the PR review comments"
        fi
        rm -f "$threads_json"
      fi
      body_file="$(mktemp)"
      {
        echo "🛑 **Auto-rework loop capped** — ${rounds_done} automatic rework rounds without an APPROVE verdict (cap: ${MAX_ROUNDS}). The machine stopped labeling \`agent:rework\`."
        echo ""
        if [ -n "$pr" ]; then
          echo "### Unresolved review threads on PR #${pr}"
          echo ""
          if [ -n "$thread_summary" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$thread_summary"
          fi
          echo ""
          echo "_If no threads are listed, the findings live in the PR general comments._"
        else
          echo "_No linked open PR found for this issue._"
        fi
        echo ""
        echo "**Next step (human):** fix the remaining findings directly and re-label \`agent:review\` for a fresh review — or re-label \`agent:rework\` to re-arm the agent loop with a fresh round cap."
      } > "$body_file"
      gh issue comment "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body_file"
      rm -f "$body_file"
      echo "→ labeled needs-human — auto-rework capped after ${rounds_done} round(s)"
      exit 0
    fi
    # agent:rework FIRST (ordering is load-bearing: the round-label
    # event must not outrank the rework queue label), then the counter.
    gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "needs-human" || true
    strip_round_labels
    gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --add-label "agent:rework"
    ensure_label "rework-round-${next_round}" "BFD4F2"
    gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --add-label "rework-round-${next_round}"
    echo "→ labeled agent:rework (round ${next_round}/${MAX_ROUNDS}) — rework run queued (re-review follows automatically)"
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ "$decision" != "approve" ]; then

    # the cycle post-review (no REQUEST_CHANGES → rework, no
    # approval → merge) with nothing but a warning line. Fail
    # LOUDLY and leave a diagnosable marker: ::error:: annotation

    echo "::error::no verdict found in any source (pr_review.json / run output / PR comments / issue comments) — the review cycle cannot be labeled (gh-305)"
    echo "→ diagnosis: ${diagnosis:-none}"
    ensure_label "needs-human" "B60205"
    gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --add-label "needs-human"
    body_file="$(mktemp)"
    {
      echo "🛑 **Review verdict missing** — the review leg finished, but no verdict (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / BLOCK) was found in any source, so the cycle cannot be labeled."
      echo ""
      echo "Per-source diagnosis: \`${diagnosis:-n/a}\`"
      echo ""

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Apply the review verdict (review runs only)) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block stays on the workflow step.
  if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    echo "::warning::SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN not set — verdict labels would not trigger workflows; skipping (a maintainer must label manually)"
    exit 0
  fi
  repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
  labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --json labels \
    --jq '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")' 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
  find_linked_pr() {
    gh pr list --repo "$repo" --state open \
      --json number,body,headRefName --jq '
      [.[] | select(
          ((.body // "") | test("(?i)\\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\\s+#'"$NUMBER"'\\b"))
          or (.headRefName | test("^'"$NUMBER"'[-_.]"))
          or (.headRefName | test("(^|[-_./])gh-0*'"$NUMBER"'$")))
        | .number] | first // empty'
  }
  pr="$(find_linked_pr)"
  # Verdict fallback sources beyond the run output (gh-305): what
  # the leg itself wrote on the PR (comments + review bodies) and
  # on the issue. A failed fetch leaves the file absent — the
  # parser's diagnosis reports it as `missing`, never a hard stop.
  verdict_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
  trap 'rm -rf "$verdict_dir"' EXIT
  pr_comments_json="${verdict_dir}/pr_comments.json"
  issue_comments_json="${verdict_dir}/issue_comments.json"
  if [ -n "$pr" ]; then
    gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$repo" --json comments,reviews \
      --jq '[(.comments // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}] + [(.reviews // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}]' \
      > "$pr_comments_json" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$pr_comments_json"
  fi
  gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --json comments \
    --jq '[(.comments // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}]' \
    > "$issue_comments_json" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$issue_comments_json"

  # deployments that set the per-repo .dmtools/config.js knob but
  # not the workflow input. Best-effort — empty on miss (then only
  # *[bot] comment authors are trusted).
  if [ -z "${MACHINE_AUTHOR:-}" ] && [ -r .dmtools/config.js ]; then
    MACHINE_AUTHOR="$(sed -nE 's/.*machineAuthor["'\'']?[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*["'\'']([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)["'\''].*/\1/p' .dmtools/config.js | head -1)"
  fi
  # Wave 2 (owner 2026-10-01): the verdict logic versions WITH the
  # reviewed pack — the unpacked pack's loop/verdict.sh WINS; the
  # legacy delegation `bash factory-agents/setup/review-verdict.sh decide`
  # remains the fallback for old pins. The pack cache
  # (~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/) is guaranteed populated
  # here: the agent run above resolved the review pack parent.
  VERDICT_SH="${FACTORY_ROOT}/setup/review-verdict.sh"
  review_agent="$(basename "${CONFIG}" .json)"
  pack_verdict="$(ls -1 "${HOME}"/.dmtools/packs/"${review_agent}"-*/loop/verdict.sh 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1 || true)"
  if [ -n "${pack_verdict}" ]; then
    VERDICT_SH="${pack_verdict}"
    echo "→ verdict logic: pack ${VERDICT_SH}"
  else
    echo "→ verdict logic: legacy tree ${VERDICT_SH} (no ${review_agent} pack loop/verdict.sh unpacked)"
  fi
  # Decision (pure logic, eval-safe key=value output): decision,
  # source, override, blocking_markers, rounds_done, next_round,
  # escalate, round_labels, diagnosis.
  eval "$(MAX_ROUNDS="${MAX_ROUNDS}" \
    PR_REVIEW_JSON="outputs/pr_review.json" \
    PR_REVIEW_JSON_ALT="outputs/gh-${NUMBER}/pr_review.json" \
    RUN_OUTPUT="${RUN_OUTPUT}" \
    PR_COMMENTS_JSON="${pr_comments_json}" \
    ISSUE_COMMENTS_JSON="${issue_comments_json}" \
    MACHINE_AUTHOR="${MACHINE_AUTHOR:-}" \
    ISSUE_LABELS="${labels}" \
    bash "${VERDICT_SH}" decide)"
  decision="${decision:-unknown}"
  escalate="${escalate:-false}"
  rounds_done="${rounds_done:-0}"
  next_round="${next_round:-0}"
  echo "→ review decision: ${decision} (source=${source:-none}, override=${override:-false}, rounds_done=${rounds_done})"
  strip_round_labels() {
    for lbl in ${round_labels:-}; do
      gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "$lbl" || true
    done
  }
  # bash -e: a missing label would abort the verdict transition —
  # create-or-update first (--force is an idempotent no-op).
  ensure_label() {
    gh label create "$1" --repo "$repo" --color "$2" --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  }

    if [ "$escalate" = "true" ]; then
      strip_round_labels
      ensure_label "needs-human" "B60205"
      gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --add-label "needs-human"
      thread_summary=""
      if [ -n "$pr" ]; then
        owner="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY%%/*}"
        name="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}"
        threads_json="$(mktemp)"
        if gh api graphql \
          -f query='query($owner:String!,$name:String!,$number:Int!){repository(owner:$owner,name:$name){pullRequest(number:$number){reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{isResolved path line comments(first:1){nodes{body author{login}}}}}}}}' \
          -f owner="$owner" -f name="$name" -F number="$pr" \
          > "$threads_json"; then
          thread_summary="$(bash "${VERDICT_SH}" threads "$threads_json")"
        else
          echo "::warning::reviewThreads fetch failed — the findings live in the PR review comments"
        fi
        rm -f "$threads_json"
      fi
      body_file="$(mktemp)"
      {
        echo "🛑 **Auto-rework loop capped** — ${rounds_done} automatic rework rounds without an APPROVE verdict (cap: ${MAX_ROUNDS}). The machine stopped labeling \`agent:rework\`."
        echo ""
        if [ -n "$pr" ]; then
          echo "### Unresolved review threads on PR #${pr}"
          echo ""
          if [ -n "$thread_summary" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$thread_summary"
          fi
          echo ""
          echo "_If no threads are listed, the findings live in the PR general comments._"
        else
          echo "_No linked open PR found for this issue._"
        fi
        echo ""
        echo "**Next step (human):** fix the remaining findings directly and re-label \`agent:review\` for a fresh review — or re-label \`agent:rework\` to re-arm the agent loop with a fresh round cap."
      } > "$body_file"
      gh issue comment "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body_file"

      exit 0
    fi

    # event must not outrank the rework queue label), then the counter.
    gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "needs-human" || true
    strip_round_labels
    gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --add-label "agent:rework"
    ensure_label "rework-round-${next_round}" "BFD4F2"
    gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --add-label "rework-round-${next_round}"
    echo "→ labeled agent:rework (round ${next_round}/${MAX_ROUNDS}) — rework run queued (re-review follows automatically)"
    exit 0
  fi

    echo "→ diagnosis: ${diagnosis:-none}"

      echo ""

 * knob is a comma-separated LIST of logins since gh-728 (owner directive

 *      for fleets where different repos run different bots.

 * @returns {string|null} the raw machine-login string (possibly a

function resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config) {

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 897
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/897
- **Title**: feat(factory): port applyReviewVerdict orchestration to JS (WIP, layer 1 green)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `refactor/factory-review-verdict-js` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +1749
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T16:28:17Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T16:28:17Z

## PR Description

## What

Ports the awf `factory-teammate.yml` «Apply the review verdict (review runs only)» step to dmtools-agents as CommonJS agent code — the keystone block of the sh→JS factory migration (policy: all factory domain logic → js/factory/, awf becomes thin plumbing; sh + A/B harness stay intact in awf until the final rewire PR).

- `js/factory/review_verdict.js` — the orchestration: fallback-source fetches (pack `loop/verdict.sh` wins, legacy `setup/review-verdict.sh` fallback), machineAuthor resolution, eval-safe key=value contract parse, label transitions, escalation comment + GraphQL review-threads query, CI-green poll gate (≤10 min), loud no-verdict path (gh-305).
- `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js` — JSRunner entry (`dmtools run`), resolveParams customParams>env>defaults, exit-1 on the loud no-verdict path.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — TDD suite, **30/30 green**.
- `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — jq-aware gh-stub parity harness: runs the REAL sh spec (byte-verbatim snapshot of awf scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ #34) and the JS side through the SAME stub world, byte-compares gh_calls.log argv, graphql payload, posted comment bytes, rc, warn lines.

## Layer plan

1. **Layer 1 — APPROVE path** (verdict extraction → CI poll → pr_approved latch): target 100% byte parity.
2. **Layer 2 — CHANGES/rework rc semantics** (re-label agent:rework under cap, round-label strip).
3. **Layer 3 — escalation / needs-human / poll-deadline loops** (cap → needs-human + threads comment, pending-forever deadline invariants).

## Current counts (updated as layers go green)

- unit: 30/30
- parity: RUNNING — counts will be updated in this body per layer (scenario classes: deterministic 7 + randomized 100).

## Harness notes (this session)

- stub rollup branch: poll-counter + CHECKS_STATE flip piped through the caller's --jq (the old mergeStateStatus case never matched the spec's argv → approve scenarios polled a real 600 s deadline).
- runSh is exec-wrapped so the 20 s SIGKILL wall kills the poll loop itself (no orphaned busy-loops); JS side gets a fake clock (+30 s/call) via the new deps.clock/deps.sleepMs seam in the entry.
- node_testRunner: scm.js preload fixed to mirror testRunner.js (makeRequire for machineNotice).

Merge gate per policy: full parity + the #889 canary leg, then the rewire PR.

```diff
diff --git a/js/factory/README.md b/js/factory/README.md
index cbac54b6..f38ff056 100644
--- a/js/factory/README.md
+++ b/js/factory/README.md
@@ -161,3 +161,85 @@ defaults (via `resolveParams`), wires `exec` → `cli_execute_command` and
 before the implementation; 37 tests) — run standalone with
 `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_factoryMarkJobDone.json`; registered in
 `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` for the Dart suite gate.
+
+### review_verdict.js — review-verdict glue (LAYER 1 PORT, WIP)
+
+JS port of the awf factory-teammate.yml step «Apply the review verdict
+(review runs only)», spec = `js/unit-tests/fixtures/apply-review-verdict.spec.sh`
+(byte-verbatim snapshot of scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ awf PR #34; the
+sh + its A/B harness stay intact there until the final rewire). Ported in
+layers per review steering:
+
+- **Layer 1 (this PR):** decision extraction (issue labels → run output →
+  linked-PR comments/reviews → issue comments), approve path
+  (pr_approved latch, needs-human removal, linked-PR guard), rework path
+  (round labels strip/add, rework-round-N creation), escalation
+  (needs-human B60205 + diagnosis comment + exit-1), verdict-logic
+  resolution (pack glob wins, legacy `$FACTORY_ROOT/setup/review-verdict.sh`
+  fallback), machineAuthor order #2 (.dmtools/config.js), loud no-verdict
+  path (gh-305: ::error:: + needs-human + per-source diagnosis + exit 1).
+- **Layer 2 (follow-up):** poll/deadline loop for pending checks
+  (10 min, bounded sleeps) — deadline-compressed parity scenario in the
+  harness already proves loop invariants.
+- **Layer 3 (follow-up):** graphql review-threads summary transport.
+
+Bugs the sh-parity harness caught in the port (pinned by tests):
+- the pr-list jq program must carry DOUBLE backslashes (`\\b`, `\\s`)
+  exactly like the sh's double-quoted string — a lone `\s` is an invalid jq
+  string escape and real gh silently empties find_linked_pr;
+- a failing verdict probe is `eval "$(cmd)"` semantics: empty output →
+  decision=unknown → the LOUD path, never a transport abort;
+- exec unwrap: an empty-output result object is an empty output, not
+  `'[object Object]'` (the pilot's `(res.output || res.stdout) || res`
+  pattern stringified the object; fix landed in this entry + module).
+
+### Env/file contract (what the awf side passes today)
+
+| env name              | param        | meaning                                     | default                       |
+|-----------------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|
+| `NUMBER`              | `number`     | the factory issue number                    | — (nothing to apply)          |
+| `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`   | `repo`       | `owner/repo`                                | — (gh call fails loud)        |
+| `RUN_OUTPUT`          | `runOutput`  | the review leg's run output file            | `.dmtools/run-output.txt`     |
+| `MAX_ROUNDS`          | `maxRounds`  | auto-rework cap before needs-human          | sh default (empty)            |
+| `CONFIG`              | `config`     | agent config file name (pack resolution)    | — (legacy tree fallback)      |
+| `FACTORY_ROOT`        | `factoryRoot`| legacy `setup/review-verdict.sh` root       | — (pack glob only)            |
+| `HOME`                | `home`       | pack cache root (`~/.dmtools/packs/`)       | — (legacy tree fallback)      |
+| `GH_TOKEN`            | `ghToken`    | must be set or the step skips (no-token)    | — (skip with ::warning::)     |
+| `MACHINE_AUTHOR`      | `machineAuthor`| trusted non-[bot] comment author          | `.dmtools/config.js` lookup   |
+| (temp) `RUN_OUTPUT`-relative | (tempFile) | staged comment/threads bodies           | `<runOutput-dir>/rv-N-*.md`   |
+
+Files touched: temp comment/threads bodies only; transports are gh
+(`gh issue view/edit`, `gh pr view/list`, `gh label create`, `gh api
+graphql` in layer 3) plus `bash "$VERDICT_SH" decide` for the pack's
+verdict logic — identical argv shapes to the sh step.
+
+### review_verdict_publish.js — JSRunner entry
+
+`action(params, deps)` glue: resolves customParams → env → defaults, wires
+`exec` → `cli_execute_command` (execOut unwrap, no trim, empty-output-safe),
+`file_write`/`file_read`, calls `applyReviewVerdict`, logs the sh's lines
+plus `⚖️ review verdict: <status>` and returns

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted byte-for-byte from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Apply the review verdict (review runs only)) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Behavior contract: identical. Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default
# shell for inline `run:`); env block stays on the workflow step.
  if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    echo "::warning::SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN not set — verdict labels would not trigger workflows; skipping (a maintainer must label manually)"
    exit 0
  fi
  repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
  labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --json labels \
    --jq '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")' 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
  find_linked_pr() {
    gh pr list --repo "$repo" --state open \
      --json number,body,headRefName --jq '
      [.[] | select(
          ((.body // "") | test("(?i)\\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\\s+#'"$NUMBER"'\\b"))
          or (.headRefName | test("^'"$NUMBER"'[-_.]"))
          or (.headRefName | test("(^|[-_./])gh-0*'"$NUMBER"'$")))
        | .number] | first // empty'
  }
  pr="$(find_linked_pr)"
  # Verdict fallback sources beyond the run output (gh-305): what
  # the leg itself wrote on the PR (comments + review bodies) and
  # on the issue. A failed fetch leaves the file absent — the
  # parser's diagnosis reports it as `missing`, never a hard stop.
  verdict_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
  trap 'rm -rf "$verdict_dir"' EXIT
  pr_comments_json="${verdict_dir}/pr_comments.json"
  issue_comments_json="${verdict_dir}/issue_comments.json"
  if [ -n "$pr" ]; then
    gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$repo" --json comments,reviews \
      --jq '[(.comments // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}] + [(.reviews // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}]' \
      > "$pr_comments_json" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$pr_comments_json"
  fi
  gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --json comments \
    --jq '[(.comments // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}]' \
    > "$issue_comments_json" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$issue_comments_json"
  # machineAuthor resolution order #2 (js/common/machineAuthor.js):
  # deployments that set the per-repo .dmtools/config.js knob but
  # not the workflow input. Best-effort — empty on miss (then only
  # *[bot] comment authors are trusted).
  if [ -z "${MACHINE_AUTHOR:-}" ] && [ -r .dmtools/config.js ]; then
    MACHINE_AUTHOR="$(sed -nE 's/.*machineAuthor["'\'']?[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*["'\'']([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)["'\''].*/\1/p' .dmtools/config.js | head -1)"
  fi
  # Wave 2 (owner 2026-10-01): the verdict logic versions WITH the
  # reviewed pack — the unpacked pack's loop/verdict.sh WINS; the
  # legacy delegation `bash factory-agents/setup/review-verdict.sh decide`
  # remains the fallback for old pins. The pack cache
  # (~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/) is guaranteed populated
  # here: the agent run above resolved the review pack parent.
  VERDICT_SH="${FACTORY_ROOT}/setup/review-verdict.sh"
  review_agent="$(basename "${CONFIG}" .json)"
  pack_verdict="$(ls -1 "${HOME}"/.dmtools/packs/"${review_agent}"-*/loop/verdict.sh 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1 || true)"
  if [ -n "${pack_verdict}" ]; then
    VERDICT_SH="${pack_verdict}"
    echo "→ verdict logic: pack ${VERDICT_SH}"
  else
    echo "→ verdict logic: legacy tree ${VERDICT_SH} (no ${review_agent} pack loop/verdict.sh unpacked)"
  fi
  # Decision (pure logic, eval-safe key=value output): decision,
  # source, override, blocking_markers, rounds_done, next_round,
  # escalate, round_labels, diagnosis.
  eval "$(MAX_ROUNDS="${MAX_ROUNDS}" \
    PR_REVIEW_JSON="outputs/pr_review.json" \
    PR_REVIEW_JSON_ALT="outputs/gh-${NUMBER}/pr_review.json" \
    RUN_OUTPUT="${RUN_OUTPUT}" \
    PR_COMMENTS_JSON="${pr_comments_json}" \
    ISSUE_COMMENTS_JSON="${issue_comments_json}" \
    MACHINE_AUTHOR="${MACHINE_AUTHOR:-}" \
    ISSUE_LABELS="${labels}" \
    bash "${VERDICT_SH}" decide)"
  decision="${decision:-unknown}"
  escalate="${escalate:-false}"
  rounds_done="${rounds_done:-0}"
  next_round="${next_round:-0}"
  echo "→ review decision: ${decision} (source=${source:-none}, override=${override:-false}, rounds_done=${rounds_done})"
  strip_round_labels() {
    for lbl in ${round_labels:-}; do
      gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "$lbl" || true
    done
  }
  # bash -e: a missing label would abort the verdict transition —
  # create-or-update first (--force is an idempotent no-op).
  ensure_label() {
    gh label create "$1" --repo "$repo" --color "$2" --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  }
  if [ "$decision" = "rework" ]; then
    if [ "$escalate" = "true" ]; then
      strip_round_labels
      ensure_label "needs-human" "B60205"
      gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --add-label "needs-human"
      thread_summary=""
      if [ -n "$pr" ]; then
        owner="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY%%/*}"
        name="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}"
        threads_json="$(mktemp)"
        if gh api graphql \
          -f query='query($owner:String!,$name:String!,$number:Int!){repository(owner:$owner,name:$name){pullRequest(number:$number){reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{isResolved path line comments(first:1){nodes{body author{login}}}}}}}}' \
          -f owner="$owner" -f name="$name" -F number="$pr" \
          > "$threads_json"; then
          thread_summary="$(bash "${VERDICT_SH}" threads "$threads_json")"
        else
          echo "::warning::reviewThreads fetch failed — the findings live in the PR review comments"
        fi
        rm -f "$threads_json"
      fi
      body_file="$(mktemp)"
      {
        echo "🛑 **Auto-rework loop capped** — ${rounds_done} automatic rework rounds without an APPROVE verdict (cap: ${MAX_ROUNDS}). The machine stopped labeling \`agent:rework\`."
        echo ""
        if [ -n "$pr" ]; then
          echo "### Unresolved review threads on PR #${pr}"
          echo ""
          if [ -n "$thread_summary" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$thread_summary"
          fi
          echo ""
          echo "_If no threads are listed, the findings live in the PR general comments._"
        else
          echo "_No linked open PR found for this issue._"
        fi
        echo ""
        echo "**Next step (human):** fix the remaining findings directly and re-label \`agent:review\` for a fresh review — or re-label \`agent:rework\` to re-arm the agent loop with a fresh round cap."
      } > "$body_file"
      gh issue comment "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body_file"
      rm -f "$body_file"
      echo "→ labeled needs-human — auto-rework capped after ${rounds_done} round(s)"
      exit 0
    fi
    # agent:rework FIRST (ordering is load-bearing: the round-label
    # event must not outrank the rework queue label), then the counter.
    gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "needs-human" || true
    strip_round_labels
    gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --add-label "agent:rework"
    ensure_label "rework-round-${next_round}" "BFD4F2"
    gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --add-label "rework-round-${next_round}"
    echo "→ labeled agent:rework (round ${next_round}/${MAX_ROUNDS}) — rework run queued (re-review follows automatically)"
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ "$decision" != "approve" ]; then
    # gh-305: the old `::warning:: … skipping labeling` STRANDED
    # the cycle post-review (no REQUEST_CHANGES → rework, no
    # approval → merge) with nothing but a warning line. Fail
    # LOUDLY and leave a diagnosable marker: ::error:: annotation
    # (red step), needs-human label, per-source diagnosis comment.

Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

## What

Ports the awf `factory-teammate.yml` «Apply the review verdict (review runs only)» step to dmtools-agents as CommonJS agent code — the keystone block of the sh→JS factory migration (policy: all factory domain logic → js/factory/, awf becomes thin plumbing; sh + A/B harness stay intact in awf until the final rewire PR).

- `js/factory/review_verdict.js` — the orchestration: fallback-source fetches (pack `loop/verdict.sh` wins, legacy `setup/review-verdict.sh` fallback), machineAuthor resolution, eval-safe key=value contract parse, label transitions, escalation comment + GraphQL review-threads query, CI-green poll gate (≤10 min), loud no-verdict path (gh-305).
- `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js` — JSRunner entry (`dmtools run`), resolveParams customParams>env>defaults, exit-1 on the loud no-verdict path.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — TDD suite, **30/30 green**.
- `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — jq-aware gh-stub parity harness: runs the REAL sh spec (byte-verbatim snapshot of awf scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ #34) and the JS side through the SAME stub world, byte-compares gh_calls.log argv, graphql payload, posted comment bytes, rc, warn lines.

## Layer plan

1. **Layer 1 — APPROVE path** (verdict extraction → CI poll → pr_approved latch): target 100% byte parity.
2. **Layer 2 — CHANGES/rework rc semantics** (re-label agent:rework under cap, round-label strip).
3. **Layer 3 — escalation / needs-human / poll-deadline loops** (cap → needs-human + threads comment, pending-forever deadline invariants).

## Current counts (updated as layers go green)

- unit: 30/30
- parity: RUNNING — counts will be updated in this body per layer (scenario classes: deterministic 7 + randomized 100).

## Harness notes (this session)

- stub rollup branch: poll-counter + CHECKS_STATE flip piped through the caller's --jq (the old mergeStateStatus case never matched the spec's argv → approve scenarios polled a real 600 s deadline).
- runSh is exec-wrapped so the 20 s SIGKILL wall kills the poll loop itself (no orphaned busy-loops); JS side gets a fake clock (+30 s/call) via the new deps.clock/deps.sleepMs seam in the entry.
- node_testRunner: scm.js preload fixed to mirror testRunner.js (makeRequire for machineNotice).

Merge gate per policy: full parity + the #889 canary leg, then the rewire PR.
