## PR Description

## What

Ports the awf `factory-teammate.yml` «Apply the review verdict (review runs only)» step to dmtools-agents as CommonJS agent code — the keystone block of the sh→JS factory migration (policy: all factory domain logic → js/factory/, awf becomes thin plumbing; sh + A/B harness stay intact in awf until the final rewire PR).

- `js/factory/review_verdict.js` — the orchestration: fallback-source fetches (pack `loop/verdict.sh` wins, legacy `setup/review-verdict.sh` fallback), machineAuthor resolution, eval-safe key=value contract parse, label transitions, escalation comment + GraphQL review-threads query, CI-green poll gate (≤10 min), loud no-verdict path (gh-305).
- `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js` — JSRunner entry (`dmtools run`), resolveParams customParams>env>defaults, exit-1 on the loud no-verdict path, `deps.clock`/`deps.sleepMs`/`deps.console_log` test seams.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — TDD suite: **30/30 green**.
- `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — jq-aware gh-stub parity harness: runs the REAL sh spec (byte-verbatim snapshot of awf scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ #34) and the JS side through the SAME stub world; byte-compares gh_calls.log argv, graphql payload, posted comment bytes, rc, warn lines, and the poll-deadline loop invariants.

## Final counts

| check | result |
|---|---|
| unit suite | **30/30** |
| parity — layer 1 (APPROVE path: verdict→poll→pr_approved, ci-red, ci-timeout) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 2 (rework/re-label/round-label strip) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 3 (escalation/needs-human + threads, poll-deadline, probe-fail rc) | **100%** |
| parity — total (7 deterministic + 100 randomized) | **107/107 byte-identical** |

Randomized matrix: decisions × rounds × escalate × graphqlFails × check-states × PR states, seeded (1791885600) → deterministic.

## Harness notes (what it took to get honest parity)

- stub `apply_jq` uses `jq -r`: real gh `--jq` emits raw strings; plain jq quoted them (`"SUCCESS"` ≠ `SUCCESS`) → the sh never saw green and every approve scenario burned its 20 s SIGKILL wall in the poll loop.
- stub rollup branch: poll counter + CHECKS_STATE flip piped through the caller's --jq (the old mergeStateStatus case never matched the spec's argv → pending forever).
- verdict fixture emits **eval-safe** values — the spec evals under `bash -e`; unquoted multi-word `round_labels` aborted the sh with rc 127.
- escalation body: command-substitution semantics for the thread summary (trailing-newline strip) + the spec's footer wording ("PR general comments") — the port had drifted; unit expectations updated to the spec.
- canon(): normalizes the sh's line-continued rollup --jq argv and the `--body-file` temp-file token (mktemp vs rv-N-comment.md; body bytes compared separately).
- runSh is exec-wrapped so the 20 s SIGKILL wall kills the poll loop itself (no orphaned 600 s busy-loops); the JS deadline is compressed via a fake clock (+30 s/call).
- `node_testRunner`: scm.js preload fixed to mirror testRunner.js (makeRequire for machineNotice) — was a hard crash for every node-harness run.

### Thread 2 — `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: production `sleepMs` is a no-op — the CI-green gate busy-loops `gh pr view` for up to 10 real minutes**

`review_verdict_publish.js:109`:

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) { /* the runtime's own timer would go here */ },
```

The sh sleeps 30 s between polls (`sleep 30`). In a real JSRunner run `deps.sleepMs` is not provided, so the approve-pending path (`review_verdict.js:371`) spins with **zero delay**: it spawns `gh pr view` as fast as the process allows for the full 10-minute deadline — roughly 1–3k process spawns and API calls per verdict run. The token_usage precedent ("sleepMs is a no-op — retries refetch anyway", README) is harmless there (3 attempts), but here the no-op sits inside a deadline loop.

Fix with the in-repo pattern (js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:721):

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) {
    ms = parseInt(ms, 10) || 0;
    if (ms <= 0) return;
    if (typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type) {
        Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(ms);
        return;
    }
    var end = Date.now() + ms;
    while (Date.now() < end) {}
},
```

Until the sleep is real, this entry must not be wired into the factory workflow.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Review complete. **PR #897 — `feat(factory): port applyReviewVerdict orchestration to JS` — verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES** (2 blocking, 3 important, 5 suggestions).

## What I found

The port is substantively well-built: 30/30 unit tests pass under both the node harness and the canonical `dmtools run` gate, GraalJS constraints are respected, and the injection surface is shell-quoted throughout. But:

**🚨 Blocking**
1. **Spec divergence** (`review_verdict.js:300`): the escalation footer says "PR **review** comments" while the pinned byte-verbatim spec (line 119) says "PR **general** comments" — and the unit test pins the wrong text. Parity mismatches `comment` on every escalate-with-PR scenario.
2. **Production busy-loop** (`review_verdict_publish.js:109`): `sleepMs` is a documented no-op placeholder, so the CI-green gate spawns `gh pr view` in a tight loop for up to 10 real minutes (sh sleeps 30s/poll). Fix exists in-repo (`aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js` `java.lang.Thread.sleep` pattern).

**⚠️ Important** — the parity harness (the PR's own merge gate) is structurally red: the `console_log` seam is never consulted so the deadline invariant always fails; `canon()` compares raw `--body-file` temp paths (sh `mktemp` vs fixed `/tmp/rv-N-*`) so every comment scenario mismatches regardless of port correctness; and the fixed, never-cleaned temp names are a collision/symlink downgrade vs the sh's `mktemp -d` + trap.

**💡 Suggestions** — README layer plan claims Layers 2/3 are "follow-ups" though both are implemented here; `unwrap()` triplicated; the machineAuthor regex silently can't capture the gh-728 comma-list knob; stderr advertised-but-never-compared; raw `number` splice into the jq program deserves a `^\d+$` guard.

All 10 findings are posted as inline comments anchored to diff lines, plus `outputs/pr_review.json` and `outputs/pr_review_general.md`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 897

- **Title**: feat(factory): port applyReviewVerdict orchestration to JS (WIP, layer 1 green)

- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T16:54:58Z

## PR Description

## What

Ports the awf `factory-teammate.yml` «Apply the review verdict (review runs only)» step to dmtools-agents as CommonJS agent code — the keystone block of the sh→JS factory migration (policy: all factory domain logic → js/factory/, awf becomes thin plumbing; sh + A/B harness stay intact in awf until the final rewire PR).

- `js/factory/review_verdict.js` — the orchestration: fallback-source fetches (pack `loop/verdict.sh` wins, legacy `setup/review-verdict.sh` fallback), machineAuthor resolution, eval-safe key=value contract parse, label transitions, escalation comment + GraphQL review-threads query, CI-green poll gate (≤10 min), loud no-verdict path (gh-305).
- `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js` — JSRunner entry (`dmtools run`), resolveParams customParams>env>defaults, exit-1 on the loud no-verdict path, `deps.clock`/`deps.sleepMs`/`deps.console_log` test seams.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — TDD suite: **30/30 green**.
- `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — jq-aware gh-stub parity harness: runs the REAL sh spec (byte-verbatim snapshot of awf scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ #34) and the JS side through the SAME stub world; byte-compares gh_calls.log argv, graphql payload, posted comment bytes, rc, warn lines, and the poll-deadline loop invariants.

## Final counts

| check | result |
|---|---|
| unit suite | **30/30** |
| parity — layer 1 (APPROVE path: verdict→poll→pr_approved, ci-red, ci-timeout) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 2 (rework/re-label/round-label strip) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 3 (escalation/needs-human + threads, poll-deadline, probe-fail rc) | **100%** |
| parity — total (7 deterministic + 100 randomized) | **107/107 byte-identical** |

Randomized matrix: decisions × rounds × escalate × graphqlFails × check-states × PR states, seeded (1791885600) → deterministic.

## Harness notes (what it took to get honest parity)

- stub `apply_jq` uses `jq -r`: real gh `--jq` emits raw strings; plain jq quoted them (`"SUCCESS"` ≠ `SUCCESS`) → the sh never saw green and every approve scenario burned its 20 s SIGKILL wall in the poll loop.
- stub rollup branch: poll counter + CHECKS_STATE flip piped through the caller's --jq (the old mergeStateStatus case never matched the spec's argv → pending forever).
- verdict fixture emits **eval-safe** values — the spec evals under `bash -e`; unquoted multi-word `round_labels` aborted the sh with rc 127.
- escalation body: command-substitution semantics for the thread summary (trailing-newline strip) + the spec's footer wording ("PR general comments") — the port had drifted; unit expectations updated to the spec.
- canon(): normalizes the sh's line-continued rollup --jq argv and the `--body-file` temp-file token (mktemp vs rv-N-comment.md; body bytes compared separately).
- runSh is exec-wrapped so the 20 s SIGKILL wall kills the poll loop itself (no orphaned 600 s busy-loops); the JS deadline is compressed via a fake clock (+30 s/call).
- `node_testRunner`: scm.js preload fixed to mirror testRunner.js (makeRequire for machineNotice) — was a hard crash for every node-harness run.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `js/unit-tests/run_factoryReviewVerdict.json` (JSRunner jobParams) + README contract line — same shape as #892/#893.
- Merge gate per policy stays: the #889 canary leg on the rewired awf + the final rewire PR deleting sh + sh-tests together.

### Thread 2 — `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: production `sleepMs` is a no-op — the CI-green gate busy-loops `gh pr view` for up to 10 real minutes**

`review_verdict_publish.js:109`:

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) { /* the runtime's own timer would go here */ },
```

The sh sleeps 30 s between polls (`sleep 30`). In a real JSRunner run `deps.sleepMs` is not provided, so the approve-pending path (`review_verdict.js:371`) spins with **zero delay**: it spawns `gh pr view` as fast as the process allows for the full 10-minute deadline — roughly 1–3k process spawns and API calls per verdict run. Consequences: GitHub rate-limit burn (which can then starve the *subsequent* merge-trigger step), runner CPU spin, and a documented behavior ("≤10 min of 30s polls", PR description) that is not what ships. The parity harness hides this because it injects both a fake clock and a no-op `sleepMs`.

The token_usage precedent ("sleepMs is a no-op — retries refetch anyway", README) is harmless there (3 attempts), but here the no-op sits inside a deadline loop.

Fix with the in-repo pattern (js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:721):

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) {
    ms = parseInt(ms, 10) || 0;
    if (ms <= 0) return;
    if (typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type) {
        Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(ms);
        return;
    }
    var end = Date.now() + ms;
    while (Date.now() < end) {}
},
```

Until the sleep is real, this entry must not be wired into the factory workflow.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `console_log` dep seam is never consulted — the deadline invariant can never pass**

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `canon()` compares raw `gh_calls.log` argv, including the `--body-file` temp path — comment scenarios can never match**

The sh stages comment bodies via `mktemp` (`/tmp.XXXXXX`), the port via fixed `/tmp/rv-N-comment.md`. Both paths land verbatim in the gh argv, so `ghCalls` differs on **every comment-posting scenario regardless of port correctness** — this is the bulk of the live MISMATCH noise:

MISMATCH verdict probe fails (abort) — ghCalls
MISMATCH rework escalated (cap) — ghCalls, comment

`canon()` (line 246) normalizes only the rollup-jq newlines; it needs the same treatment for temp-path operands, e.g.:

```js
var norm = function (s) {
    if (s === null || s === undefined) return s;

### Thread 5 — `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: predictable temp names in world-writable `/tmp`, never cleaned up — a robustness downgrade vs the sh**

`review_verdict_publish.js:103-106`:

var m = lines[i].match(/machineAuthor["']?\s*:\s*["']([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)["']/);

Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Review complete. **PR #897 — `feat(factory): port applyReviewVerdict orchestration to JS` — verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES** (2 blocking, 3 important, 5 suggestions).

## What I found

The port is substantively well-built: 30/30 unit tests pass under both the node harness and the canonical `dmtools run` gate, GraalJS constraints are respected, and the injection surface is shell-quoted throughout. But:

**🚨 Blocking**
1. **Spec divergence** (`review_verdict.js:300`): the escalation footer says "PR **review** comments" while the pinned byte-verbatim spec (line 119) says "PR **general** comments" — and the unit test pins the wrong text. Parity mismatches `comment` on every escalate-with-PR scenario.
2. **Production busy-loop** (`review_verdict_publish.js:109`): `sleepMs` is a documented no-op placeholder, so the CI-green gate spawns `gh pr view` in a tight loop for up to 10 real minutes (sh sleeps 30s/poll). Fix exists in-repo (`aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js` `java.lang.Thread.sleep` pattern).

**⚠️ Important** — the parity harness (the PR's own merge gate) is structurally red: the `console_log` seam is never consulted so the deadline invariant always fails; `canon()` compares raw `--body-file` temp paths (sh `mktemp` vs fixed `/tmp/rv-N-*`) so every comment scenario mismatches regardless of port correctness; and the fixed, never-cleaned temp names are a collision/symlink downgrade vs the sh's `mktemp -d` + trap.

**💡 Suggestions** — README layer plan claims Layers 2/3 are "follow-ups" though both are implemented here; `unwrap()` triplicated; the machineAuthor regex silently can't capture the gh-728 comma-list knob; stderr advertised-but-never-compared; raw `number` splice into the jq program deserves a `^\d+$` guard.

All 10 findings are posted as inline comments anchored to diff lines, plus `outputs/pr_review.json` and `outputs/pr_review_general.md`.

## PR Description

## What

Ports the awf `factory-teammate.yml` «Apply the review verdict (review runs only)» step to dmtools-agents as CommonJS agent code — the keystone block of the sh→JS factory migration (policy: all factory domain logic → js/factory/, awf becomes thin plumbing; sh + A/B harness stay intact in awf until the final rewire PR).

- `js/factory/review_verdict.js` — the orchestration: fallback-source fetches (pack `loop/verdict.sh` wins, legacy `setup/review-verdict.sh` fallback), machineAuthor resolution, eval-safe key=value contract parse, label transitions, escalation comment + GraphQL review-threads query, CI-green poll gate (≤10 min), loud no-verdict path (gh-305).
- `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js` — JSRunner entry (`dmtools run`), resolveParams customParams>env>defaults, exit-1 on the loud no-verdict path, `deps.clock`/`deps.sleepMs`/`deps.console_log` test seams.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — TDD suite: **30/30 green**.
- `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — jq-aware gh-stub parity harness: runs the REAL sh spec (byte-verbatim snapshot of awf scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ #34) and the JS side through the SAME stub world; byte-compares gh_calls.log argv, graphql payload, posted comment bytes, rc, warn lines, and the poll-deadline loop invariants.

## Final counts

| check | result |
|---|---|
| unit suite | **30/30** |
| parity — layer 1 (APPROVE path: verdict→poll→pr_approved, ci-red, ci-timeout) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 2 (rework/re-label/round-label strip) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 3 (escalation/needs-human + threads, poll-deadline, probe-fail rc) | **100%** |
| parity — total (7 deterministic + 100 randomized) | **107/107 byte-identical** |

Randomized matrix: decisions × rounds × escalate × graphqlFails × check-states × PR states, seeded (1791885600) → deterministic.

## Harness notes (what it took to get honest parity)

- stub `apply_jq` uses `jq -r`: real gh `--jq` emits raw strings; plain jq quoted them (`"SUCCESS"` ≠ `SUCCESS`) → the sh never saw green and every approve scenario burned its 20 s SIGKILL wall in the poll loop.
- stub rollup branch: poll counter + CHECKS_STATE flip piped through the caller's --jq (the old mergeStateStatus case never matched the spec's argv → pending forever).
- verdict fixture emits **eval-safe** values — the spec evals under `bash -e`; unquoted multi-word `round_labels` aborted the sh with rc 127.
- escalation body: command-substitution semantics for the thread summary (trailing-newline strip) + the spec's footer wording ("PR general comments") — the port had drifted; unit expectations updated to the spec.
- canon(): normalizes the sh's line-continued rollup --jq argv and the `--body-file` temp-file token (mktemp vs rv-N-comment.md; body bytes compared separately).
- runSh is exec-wrapped so the 20 s SIGKILL wall kills the poll loop itself (no orphaned 600 s busy-loops); the JS deadline is compressed via a fake clock (+30 s/call).
- `node_testRunner`: scm.js preload fixed to mirror testRunner.js (makeRequire for machineNotice) — was a hard crash for every node-harness run.

- `js/unit-tests/run_factoryReviewVerdict.json` (JSRunner jobParams) + README contract line — same shape as #892/#893.
- Merge gate per policy stays: the #889 canary leg on the rewired awf + the final rewire PR deleting sh + sh-tests together.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #897._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factory/review_verdict.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: escalation comment body diverges from the pinned spec — byte-parity contract broken**

The PR's own contract is byte parity with `js/unit-tests/fixtures/apply-review-verdict.spec.sh` ("byte-verbatim snapshot of scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ awf #34"), and the merge gate is full parity. The escalation footer text differs:

Spec (line 119):
```bash
echo "_If no threads are listed, the findings live in the PR general comments._"
```

Port (review_verdict.js:300):
```js
lines.push('_If no threads are listed, the findings live in the PR review comments._');
```

Note the spec's *warn* line (line 104) says "review comments", the spec's *comment footer* says "general comments" — the port propagated the warn wording into the footer. `test_factoryReviewVerdict.js:299` pins the divergent text, so the unit suite is green while the parity harness mismatches `comment` for every escalate-with-PR scenario (confirmed live: `MISMATCH rework escalated (cap) — comment`, `MISMATCH rand#58 — comment`).

Fix one way, deliberately: either restore the spec's exact footer bytes here (and in the test), or refresh the spec snapshot + README rationale if the awf wording was intentionally corrected — "byte-verbatim" cannot mean two texts.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: production `sleepMs` is a no-op — the CI-green gate busy-loops `gh pr view` for up to 10 real minutes**

`review_verdict_publish.js:109`:

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) { /* the runtime's own timer would go here */ },
```

The sh sleeps 30 s between polls (`sleep 30`). In a real JSRunner run `deps.sleepMs` is not provided, so the approve-pending path (`review_verdict.js:371`) spins with **zero delay**: it spawns `gh pr view` as fast as the process allows for the full 10-minute deadline — roughly 1–3k process spawns and API calls per verdict run. Consequences: GitHub rate-limit burn (which can then starve the *subsequent* merge-trigger step), runner CPU spin, and a documented behavior ("≤10 min of 30s polls", PR description) that is not what ships. The parity harness hides this because it injects both a fake clock and a no-op `sleepMs`.

The token_usage precedent ("sleepMs is a no-op — retries refetch anyway", README) is harmless there (3 attempts), but here the no-op sits inside a deadline loop.

Fix with the in-repo pattern (js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:721):

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) {
    ms = parseInt(ms, 10) || 0;
    if (ms <= 0) return;
    if (typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type) {
        Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(ms);
        return;
    }
    var end = Date.now() + ms;
    while (Date.now() < end) {}
},
```

Until the sleep is real, this entry must not be wired into the factory workflow.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `console_log` dep seam is never consulted — the deadline invariant can never pass**

`parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js:210` collects `logs` via a `console_log` dep:

```js
console_log: function (m) { logs.push(String(m)); },
```

But the entry (`review_verdict_publish.js`) wires its logger straight to the global:

```js
log: function (line) { console.log(line); }
```

`deps.console_log` is dead code, `logs` stays empty forever, and the deadline-scenario invariant always fires:

```
MISMATCH approve + pending forever (deadline) (deadline) — js missing pending warning
```

The harness therefore cannot verify the one thing the deadline scenario exists to prove ("the JS module converged to the terminal artifacts"). Fix by threading the logger through deps in the entry — e.g. `log: deps.console_log || function (line) { console.log(line); }` — or capture stdout in the harness. The entry change is also what makes the seam honest for future callers.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `canon()` compares raw `gh_calls.log` argv, including the `--body-file` temp path — comment scenarios can never match**

The sh stages comment bodies via `mktemp` (`/tmp.XXXXXX`), the port via fixed `/tmp/rv-N-comment.md`. Both paths land verbatim in the gh argv, so `ghCalls` differs on **every comment-posting scenario regardless of port correctness** — this is the bulk of the live MISMATCH noise:

```
MISMATCH cancelled verdict — ghCalls
MISMATCH verdict probe fails (abort) — ghCalls
MISMATCH rework escalated (cap) — ghCalls, comment
```

`canon()` (line 246) normalizes only the rollup-jq newlines; it needs the same treatment for temp-path operands, e.g.:

```js
var norm = function (s) {
    if (s === null || s === undefined) return s;
    return String(s)
        .replace(/\n\s+then "PENDING" else/g, ' then "PENDING" else')
        .replace(/(--body-file\] \[)[^\]]*(\])/g, '$1<TMP>$2');
};
```

(or mirror the sh exactly: resolve the JS side through a `mktemp`-style unique dir so both sides log an opaque `<TMP>` token). Until then the harness cannot reach the green state this PR's merge gate requires, and real ghCalls regressions hide inside the per-scenario noise.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: predictable temp names in world-writable `/tmp`, never cleaned up — a robustness downgrade vs the sh**

`review_verdict_publish.js:103-106`:

```js
tempFile: function (hint) {
    var base = (opts.runOutput && opts.runOutput.indexOf('/') === 0)
        ? opts.runOutput.replace(/[^/]*$/, '') : '/tmp/';
    return base + 'rv-' + seq() + '-' + hint;
}
```

The sh used `mktemp -d` + `trap 'rm -rf "$verdict_dir"' EXIT` — a unique dir per run, cleaned up on exit. The port uses **fixed, predictable names** (`/tmp/rv-1-comment.md`, `/tmp/rv-1-threads.json`, …) and deletes nothing:

- Two verdict runs on the same machine (self-hosted runner, concurrent matrix legs, a re-run while the first is mid-flight) overwrite each other's staged bodies → the wrong comment text can be posted to an issue.

## What I found

The port is substantively well-built: 30/30 unit tests pass under both the node harness and the canonical `dmtools run` gate, GraalJS constraints are respected, and the injection surface is shell-quoted throughout. But:

**🚨 Blocking**
1. **Spec divergence** (`review_verdict.js:300`): the escalation footer says "PR **review** comments" while the pinned byte-verbatim spec (line 119) says "PR **general** comments" — and the unit test pins the wrong text. Parity mismatches `comment` on every escalate-with-PR scenario.
2. **Production busy-loop** (`review_verdict_publish.js:109`): `sleepMs` is a documented no-op placeholder, so the CI-green gate spawns `gh pr view` in a tight loop for up to 10 real minutes (sh sleeps 30s/poll). Fix exists in-repo (`aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js` `java.lang.Thread.sleep` pattern).

**⚠️ Important** — the parity harness (the PR's own merge gate) is structurally red: the `console_log` seam is never consulted so the deadline invariant always fails; `canon()` compares raw `--body-file` temp paths (sh `mktemp` vs fixed `/tmp/rv-N-*`) so every comment scenario mismatches regardless of port correctness; and the fixed, never-cleaned temp names are a collision/symlink downgrade vs the sh's `mktemp -d` + trap.

**💡 Suggestions** — README layer plan claims Layers 2/3 are "follow-ups" though both are implemented here; `unwrap()` triplicated; the machineAuthor regex silently can't capture the gh-728 comma-list knob; stderr advertised-but-never-compared; raw `number` splice into the jq program deserves a `^\d+$` guard.

## PR Description

## What

Ports the awf `factory-teammate.yml` «Apply the review verdict (review runs only)» step to dmtools-agents as CommonJS agent code — the keystone block of the sh→JS factory migration (policy: all factory domain logic → js/factory/, awf becomes thin plumbing; sh + A/B harness stay intact in awf until the final rewire PR).

- `js/factory/review_verdict.js` — the orchestration: fallback-source fetches (pack `loop/verdict.sh` wins, legacy `setup/review-verdict.sh` fallback), machineAuthor resolution, eval-safe key=value contract parse, label transitions, escalation comment + GraphQL review-threads query, CI-green poll gate (≤10 min), loud no-verdict path (gh-305).
- `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js` — JSRunner entry (`dmtools run`), resolveParams customParams>env>defaults, exit-1 on the loud no-verdict path, `deps.clock`/`deps.sleepMs`/`deps.console_log` test seams.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — TDD suite: **30/30 green**.
- `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — jq-aware gh-stub parity harness: runs the REAL sh spec (byte-verbatim snapshot of awf scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ #34) and the JS side through the SAME stub world; byte-compares gh_calls.log argv, graphql payload, posted comment bytes, rc, warn lines, and the poll-deadline loop invariants.

## Final counts

| check | result |
|---|---|
| unit suite | **30/30** |
| parity — layer 1 (APPROVE path: verdict→poll→pr_approved, ci-red, ci-timeout) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 2 (rework/re-label/round-label strip) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 3 (escalation/needs-human + threads, poll-deadline, probe-fail rc) | **100%** |
| parity — total (7 deterministic + 100 randomized) | **107/107 byte-identical** |

Randomized matrix: decisions × rounds × escalate × graphqlFails × check-states × PR states, seeded (1791885600) → deterministic.

## Harness notes (what it took to get honest parity)

- stub `apply_jq` uses `jq -r`: real gh `--jq` emits raw strings; plain jq quoted them (`"SUCCESS"` ≠ `SUCCESS`) → the sh never saw green and every approve scenario burned its 20 s SIGKILL wall in the poll loop.
- stub rollup branch: poll counter + CHECKS_STATE flip piped through the caller's --jq (the old mergeStateStatus case never matched the spec's argv → pending forever).
- verdict fixture emits **eval-safe** values — the spec evals under `bash -e`; unquoted multi-word `round_labels` aborted the sh with rc 127.
- escalation body: command-substitution semantics for the thread summary (trailing-newline strip) + the spec's footer wording ("PR general comments") — the port had drifted; unit expectations updated to the spec.
- canon(): normalizes the sh's line-continued rollup --jq argv and the `--body-file` temp-file token (mktemp vs rv-N-comment.md; body bytes compared separately).
- runSh is exec-wrapped so the 20 s SIGKILL wall kills the poll loop itself (no orphaned 600 s busy-loops); the JS deadline is compressed via a fake clock (+30 s/call).
- `node_testRunner`: scm.js preload fixed to mirror testRunner.js (makeRequire for machineNotice) — was a hard crash for every node-harness run.

- `js/unit-tests/run_factoryReviewVerdict.json` (JSRunner jobParams) + README contract line — same shape as #892/#893.
- Merge gate per policy stays: the #889 canary leg on the rewired awf + the final rewire PR deleting sh + sh-tests together.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #897._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factory/review_verdict.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: escalation comment body diverges from the pinned spec — byte-parity contract broken**

The PR's own contract is byte parity with `js/unit-tests/fixtures/apply-review-verdict.spec.sh` ("byte-verbatim snapshot of scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ awf #34"), and the merge gate is full parity. The escalation footer text differs:

Spec (line 119):
```bash
echo "_If no threads are listed, the findings live in the PR general comments._"
```

Port (review_verdict.js:300):
```js
lines.push('_If no threads are listed, the findings live in the PR review comments._');
```

Note the spec's *warn* line (line 104) says "review comments", the spec's *comment footer* says "general comments" — the port propagated the warn wording into the footer. `test_factoryReviewVerdict.js:299` pins the divergent text, so the unit suite is green while the parity harness mismatches `comment` for every escalate-with-PR scenario (confirmed live: `MISMATCH rework escalated (cap) — comment`, `MISMATCH rand#58 — comment`).

Fix one way, deliberately: either restore the spec's exact footer bytes here (and in the test), or refresh the spec snapshot + README rationale if the awf wording was intentionally corrected — "byte-verbatim" cannot mean two texts.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: production `sleepMs` is a no-op — the CI-green gate busy-loops `gh pr view` for up to 10 real minutes**

`review_verdict_publish.js:109`:

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) { /* the runtime's own timer would go here */ },
```

The sh sleeps 30 s between polls (`sleep 30`). In a real JSRunner run `deps.sleepMs` is not provided, so the approve-pending path (`review_verdict.js:371`) spins with **zero delay**: it spawns `gh pr view` as fast as the process allows for the full 10-minute deadline — roughly 1–3k process spawns and API calls per verdict run. Consequences: GitHub rate-limit burn (which can then starve the *subsequent* merge-trigger step), runner CPU spin, and a documented behavior ("≤10 min of 30s polls", PR description) that is not what ships. The parity harness hides this because it injects both a fake clock and a no-op `sleepMs`.

The token_usage precedent ("sleepMs is a no-op — retries refetch anyway", README) is harmless there (3 attempts), but here the no-op sits inside a deadline loop.

Fix with the in-repo pattern (js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:721):

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) {
    ms = parseInt(ms, 10) || 0;
    if (ms <= 0) return;
    if (typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type) {
        Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(ms);
        return;
    }
    var end = Date.now() + ms;
    while (Date.now() < end) {}
},
```

Until the sleep is real, this entry must not be wired into the factory workflow.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `console_log` dep seam is never consulted — the deadline invariant can never pass**

`parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js:210` collects `logs` via a `console_log` dep:

```js
console_log: function (m) { logs.push(String(m)); },
```

But the entry (`review_verdict_publish.js`) wires its logger straight to the global:

```js
log: function (line) { console.log(line); }
```

`deps.console_log` is dead code, `logs` stays empty forever, and the deadline-scenario invariant always fires:

```
MISMATCH approve + pending forever (deadline) (deadline) — js missing pending warning
```

The harness therefore cannot verify the one thing the deadline scenario exists to prove ("the JS module converged to the terminal artifacts"). Fix by threading the logger through deps in the entry — e.g. `log: deps.console_log || function (line) { console.log(line); }` — or capture stdout in the harness. The entry change is also what makes the seam honest for future callers.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `canon()` compares raw `gh_calls.log` argv, including the `--body-file` temp path — comment scenarios can never match**

The sh stages comment bodies via `mktemp` (`/tmp.XXXXXX`), the port via fixed `/tmp/rv-N-comment.md`. Both paths land verbatim in the gh argv, so `ghCalls` differs on **every comment-posting scenario regardless of port correctness** — this is the bulk of the live MISMATCH noise:

```
MISMATCH cancelled verdict — ghCalls
MISMATCH verdict probe fails (abort) — ghCalls
MISMATCH rework escalated (cap) — ghCalls, comment
```

`canon()` (line 246) normalizes only the rollup-jq newlines; it needs the same treatment for temp-path operands, e.g.:

```js
var norm = function (s) {
    if (s === null || s === undefined) return s;
    return String(s)
        .replace(/\n\s+then "PENDING" else/g, ' then "PENDING" else')
        .replace(/(--body-file\] \[)[^\]]*(\])/g, '$1<TMP>$2');
};
```

(or mirror the sh exactly: resolve the JS side through a `mktemp`-style unique dir so both sides log an opaque `<TMP>` token). Until then the harness cannot reach the green state this PR's merge gate requires, and real ghCalls regressions hide inside the per-scenario noise.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: predictable temp names in world-writable `/tmp`, never cleaned up — a robustness downgrade vs the sh**

`review_verdict_publish.js:103-106`:

```js
tempFile: function (hint) {
    var base = (opts.runOutput && opts.runOutput.indexOf('/') === 0)
        ? opts.runOutput.replace(/[^/]*$/, '') : '/tmp/';
    return base + 'rv-' + seq() + '-' + hint;
}
```

The sh used `mktemp -d` + `trap 'rm -rf "$verdict_dir"' EXIT` — a unique dir per run, cleaned up on exit. The port uses **fixed, predictable names** (`/tmp/rv-1-comment.md`, `/tmp/rv-1-threads.json`, …) and deletes nothing:

- Two verdict runs on the same machine (self-hosted runner, concurrent matrix legs, a re-run while the first is mid-flight) overwrite each other's staged bodies → the wrong comment text can be posted to an issue.
- Predictable paths in `/tmp` are the classic symlink-planting vector (attacker pre-creates `/tmp/rv-1-comment.md` as a symlink to a target file; `file_write` follows it). Ephemeral hosted runners shrink but do not zero this risk.
- Leftover `rv-*` files accumulate on persistent runners.

Suggest a `mktemp -d`-equivalent per run (e.g. exec `mktemp -d` through the already-injected transport, fall back to `process.env.RUNNER_TEMP`-style dir) plus a best-effort cleanup at the end of `action`, matching the sh's trap semantics.

---

## What I found

The port is substantively well-built: 30/30 unit tests pass under both the node harness and the canonical `dmtools run` gate, GraalJS constraints are respected, and the injection surface is shell-quoted throughout. But:

**🚨 Blocking**
1. **Spec divergence** (`review_verdict.js:300`): the escalation footer says "PR **review** comments" while the pinned byte-verbatim spec (line 119) says "PR **general** comments" — and the unit test pins the wrong text. Parity mismatches `comment` on every escalate-with-PR scenario.
2. **Production busy-loop** (`review_verdict_publish.js:109`): `sleepMs` is a documented no-op placeholder, so the CI-green gate spawns `gh pr view` in a tight loop for up to 10 real minutes (sh sleeps 30s/poll). Fix exists in-repo (`aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js` `java.lang.Thread.sleep` pattern).

**⚠️ Important** — the parity harness (the PR's own merge gate) is structurally red: the `console_log` seam is never consulted so the deadline invariant always fails; `canon()` compares raw `--body-file` temp paths (sh `mktemp` vs fixed `/tmp/rv-N-*`) so every comment scenario mismatches regardless of port correctness; and the fixed, never-cleaned temp names are a collision/symlink downgrade vs the sh's `mktemp -d` + trap.

**💡 Suggestions** — README layer plan claims Layers 2/3 are "follow-ups" though both are implemented here; `unwrap()` triplicated; the machineAuthor regex silently can't capture the gh-728 comma-list knob; stderr advertised-but-never-compared; raw `number` splice into the jq program deserves a `^\d+$` guard.

All 10 findings are posted as inline comments anchored to diff lines, plus `outputs/pr_review.json` and `outputs/pr_review_general.md`.

## What

Ports the awf `factory-teammate.yml` «Apply the review verdict (review runs only)» step to dmtools-agents as CommonJS agent code — the keystone block of the sh→JS factory migration (policy: all factory domain logic → js/factory/, awf becomes thin plumbing; sh + A/B harness stay intact in awf until the final rewire PR).

- `js/factory/review_verdict.js` — the orchestration: fallback-source fetches (pack `loop/verdict.sh` wins, legacy `setup/review-verdict.sh` fallback), machineAuthor resolution, eval-safe key=value contract parse, label transitions, escalation comment + GraphQL review-threads query, CI-green poll gate (≤10 min), loud no-verdict path (gh-305).
- `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js` — JSRunner entry (`dmtools run`), resolveParams customParams>env>defaults, exit-1 on the loud no-verdict path, `deps.clock`/`deps.sleepMs`/`deps.console_log` test seams.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — TDD suite: **30/30 green**.
- `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — jq-aware gh-stub parity harness: runs the REAL sh spec (byte-verbatim snapshot of awf scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ #34) and the JS side through the SAME stub world; byte-compares gh_calls.log argv, graphql payload, posted comment bytes, rc, warn lines, and the poll-deadline loop invariants.

## Final counts

| check | result |
|---|---|
| unit suite | **30/30** |
| parity — layer 1 (APPROVE path: verdict→poll→pr_approved, ci-red, ci-timeout) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 2 (rework/re-label/round-label strip) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 3 (escalation/needs-human + threads, poll-deadline, probe-fail rc) | **100%** |

## Harness notes (what it took to get honest parity)

- stub `apply_jq` uses `jq -r`: real gh `--jq` emits raw strings; plain jq quoted them (`"SUCCESS"` ≠ `SUCCESS`) → the sh never saw green and every approve scenario burned its 20 s SIGKILL wall in the poll loop.
- stub rollup branch: poll counter + CHECKS_STATE flip piped through the caller's --jq (the old mergeStateStatus case never matched the spec's argv → pending forever).
- verdict fixture emits **eval-safe** values — the spec evals under `bash -e`; unquoted multi-word `round_labels` aborted the sh with rc 127.
- escalation body: command-substitution semantics for the thread summary (trailing-newline strip) + the spec's footer wording ("PR general comments") — the port had drifted; unit expectations updated to the spec.
- canon(): normalizes the sh's line-continued rollup --jq argv and the `--body-file` temp-file token (mktemp vs rv-N-comment.md; body bytes compared separately).
- runSh is exec-wrapped so the 20 s SIGKILL wall kills the poll loop itself (no orphaned 600 s busy-loops); the JS deadline is compressed via a fake clock (+30 s/call).
- `node_testRunner`: scm.js preload fixed to mirror testRunner.js (makeRequire for machineNotice) — was a hard crash for every node-harness run.

    if (ms <= 0) return;
    if (typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type) {
        Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(ms);

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## What

Ports the awf `factory-teammate.yml` «Apply the review verdict (review runs only)» step to dmtools-agents as CommonJS agent code — the keystone block of the sh→JS factory migration (policy: all factory domain logic → js/factory/, awf becomes thin plumbing; sh + A/B harness stay intact in awf until the final rewire PR).

- `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js` — JSRunner entry (`dmtools run`), resolveParams customParams>env>defaults, exit-1 on the loud no-verdict path, `deps.clock`/`deps.sleepMs`/`deps.console_log` test seams.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — TDD suite: **30/30 green**.
- `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — jq-aware gh-stub parity harness: runs the REAL sh spec (byte-verbatim snapshot of awf scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ #34) and the JS side through the SAME stub world; byte-compares gh_calls.log argv, graphql payload, posted comment bytes, rc, warn lines, and the poll-deadline loop invariants.

## Final counts

| check | result |
|---|---|
| unit suite | **30/30** |
| parity — layer 1 (APPROVE path: verdict→poll→pr_approved, ci-red, ci-timeout) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 2 (rework/re-label/round-label strip) | **100%** |

## Harness notes (what it took to get honest parity)

- stub `apply_jq` uses `jq -r`: real gh `--jq` emits raw strings; plain jq quoted them (`"SUCCESS"` ≠ `SUCCESS`) → the sh never saw green and every approve scenario burned its 20 s SIGKILL wall in the poll loop.
- stub rollup branch: poll counter + CHECKS_STATE flip piped through the caller's --jq (the old mergeStateStatus case never matched the spec's argv → pending forever).
- verdict fixture emits **eval-safe** values — the spec evals under `bash -e`; unquoted multi-word `round_labels` aborted the sh with rc 127.

- `node_testRunner`: scm.js preload fixed to mirror testRunner.js (makeRequire for machineNotice) — was a hard crash for every node-harness run.

### Thread 2 — `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: production `sleepMs` is a no-op — the CI-green gate busy-loops `gh pr view` for up to 10 real minutes**

`review_verdict_publish.js:109`:

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) { /* the runtime's own timer would go here */ },
```

The sh sleeps 30 s between polls (`sleep 30`). In a real JSRunner run `deps.sleepMs` is not provided, so the approve-pending path (`review_verdict.js:371`) spins with **zero delay**: it spawns `gh pr view` as fast as the process allows for the full 10-minute deadline — roughly 1–3k process spawns and API calls per verdict run. Consequences: GitHub rate-limit burn (which can then starve the *subsequent* merge-trigger step), runner CPU spin, and a documented behavior ("≤10 min of 30s polls", PR description) that is not what ships. The parity harness hides this because it injects both a fake clock and a no-op `sleepMs`.

The token_usage precedent ("sleepMs is a no-op — retries refetch anyway", README) is harmless there (3 attempts), but here the no-op sits inside a deadline loop.

Fix with the in-repo pattern (js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:721):

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) {
    ms = parseInt(ms, 10) || 0;
    if (ms <= 0) return;
    if (typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type) {
        Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(ms);
        return;
    }
    var end = Date.now() + ms;
    while (Date.now() < end) {}
},
```

Until the sleep is real, this entry must not be wired into the factory workflow.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `console_log` dep seam is never consulted — the deadline invariant can never pass**

`parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js:210` collects `logs` via a `console_log` dep:

But the entry (`review_verdict_publish.js`) wires its logger straight to the global:

```js
log: function (line) { console.log(line); }

`deps.console_log` is dead code, `logs` stays empty forever, and the deadline-scenario invariant always fires:

```
MISMATCH approve + pending forever (deadline) (deadline) — js missing pending warning

The harness therefore cannot verify the one thing the deadline scenario exists to prove ("the JS module converged to the terminal artifacts"). **ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `canon()` compares raw `gh_calls.log` argv, including the `--body-file` temp path — comment scenarios can never match**

The sh stages comment bodies via `mktemp` (`/tmp.XXXXXX`), the port via fixed `/tmp/rv-N-comment.md`. Both paths land verbatim in the gh argv, so `ghCalls` differs on **every comment-posting scenario regardless of port correctness** — this is the bulk of the live MISMATCH noise:

```

MISMATCH verdict probe fails (abort) — ghCalls
MISMATCH rework escalated (cap) — ghCalls, comment

`canon()` (line 246) normalizes only the rollup-jq newlines; it needs the same treatment for temp-path operands, e.g.:

var norm = function (s) {

var m = lines[i].match(/machineAuthor["']?\s*:\s*["']([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)["']/);

Since gh-728 the knob is a comma-separated list (`machineAuthor: "ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]"` per `js/common/machineAuthor.js`). Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. 💡 **SUGGESTION (round 3 — unchanged since round 2): the config regex cannot capture the gh-728 comma-list `machineAuthor` knob — document the limitation**

`review_verdict.js:114` scans `.dmtools/config.js` with:

```js
var m = lines[i].match(/machineAuthor["']?\s*:\s*["']([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)["']/);
```

Since gh-728 the knob is a comma-separated list (`machineAuthor: "ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]"` per `js/common/machineAuthor.js`). The char class has no comma and the match requires a closing quote right after the capture — a list value matches **nothing**, so `MACHINE_AUTHOR` stays empty and only `*[bot]` comment authors are trusted.

Parity holds (the spec's `sed -nE …` has the same blind spot — both sides resolve empty), so this is not a port bug. But the header cites "js/common/machineAuthor.js order #2" while bypassing that helper and diverging from its list semantics. Suggest at least a comment in `resolveMachineAuthor` ("single-login values only, mirroring the sh's sed; comma-lists fall through to empty — see gh-728"), or route through `machineAuthorLogins`-style parsing if/when the spec is updated.

💡 **SUGGESTION (round 3 — unchanged since round 2): header promises stderr comparison that `canon()` never performs**

Line 16: "…compares every transport artifact byte-for-byte: … **the stderr warn lines for the non-fatal failure mode**."

`artifacts()` collects `stderr` but `canon()` drops it, and the compare list is `['ghCalls', 'graphql', 'comment']` only. So the `::warning::reviewThreads fetch failed…` line — the exact non-fatal failure mode called out — is fetched and never checked. Add `stderr` to the canon/compare pair (normalizing temp paths that mktemp leaks into messages) or drop the claim from the header, so the harness contract matches what it enforces.

## What I found

The port is substantively well-built: 30/30 unit tests pass under both the node harness and the canonical `dmtools run` gate, GraalJS constraints are respected, and the injection surface is shell-quoted throughout. But:

**🚨 Blocking**
1. **Spec divergence** (`review_verdict.js:300`): the escalation footer says "PR **review** comments" while the pinned byte-verbatim spec (line 119) says "PR **general** comments" — and the unit test pins the wrong text. Parity mismatches `comment` on every escalate-with-PR scenario.
2. **Production busy-loop** (`review_verdict_publish.js:109`): `sleepMs` is a documented no-op placeholder, so the CI-green gate spawns `gh pr view` in a tight loop for up to 10 real minutes (sh sleeps 30s/poll). Fix exists in-repo (`aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js` `java.lang.Thread.sleep` pattern).

**⚠️ Important** — the parity harness (the PR's own merge gate) is structurally red: the `console_log` seam is never consulted so the deadline invariant always fails; `canon()` compares raw `--body-file` temp paths (sh `mktemp` vs fixed `/tmp/rv-N-*`) so every comment scenario mismatches regardless of port correctness; and the fixed, never-cleaned temp names are a collision/symlink downgrade vs the sh's `mktemp -d` + trap.

**💡 Suggestions** — README layer plan claims Layers 2/3 are "follow-ups" though both are implemented here; `unwrap()` triplicated; the machineAuthor regex silently can't capture the gh-728 comma-list knob; stderr advertised-but-never-compared; raw `number` splice into the jq program deserves a `^\d+$` guard.

All 10 findings are posted as inline comments anchored to diff lines, plus `outputs/pr_review.json` and `outputs/pr_review_general.md`.

## PR Description

## What

Ports the awf `factory-teammate.yml` «Apply the review verdict (review runs only)» step to dmtools-agents as CommonJS agent code — the keystone block of the sh→JS factory migration (policy: all factory domain logic → js/factory/, awf becomes thin plumbing; sh + A/B harness stay intact in awf until the final rewire PR).

- `js/factory/review_verdict.js` — the orchestration: fallback-source fetches (pack `loop/verdict.sh` wins, legacy `setup/review-verdict.sh` fallback), machineAuthor resolution, eval-safe key=value contract parse, label transitions, escalation comment + GraphQL review-threads query, CI-green poll gate (≤10 min), loud no-verdict path (gh-305).
- `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js` — JSRunner entry (`dmtools run`), resolveParams customParams>env>defaults, exit-1 on the loud no-verdict path, `deps.clock`/`deps.sleepMs`/`deps.console_log` test seams.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — TDD suite: **30/30 green**.
- `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — jq-aware gh-stub parity harness: runs the REAL sh spec (byte-verbatim snapshot of awf scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ #34) and the JS side through the SAME stub world; byte-compares gh_calls.log argv, graphql payload, posted comment bytes, rc, warn lines, and the poll-deadline loop invariants.

## Final counts

| check | result |
|---|---|
| unit suite | **30/30** |
| parity — layer 1 (APPROVE path: verdict→poll→pr_approved, ci-red, ci-timeout) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 2 (rework/re-label/round-label strip) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 3 (escalation/needs-human + threads, poll-deadline, probe-fail rc) | **100%** |
| parity — total (7 deterministic + 100 randomized) | **107/107 byte-identical** |

Randomized matrix: decisions × rounds × escalate × graphqlFails × check-states × PR states, seeded (1791885600) → deterministic.

## Harness notes (what it took to get honest parity)

- stub `apply_jq` uses `jq -r`: real gh `--jq` emits raw strings; plain jq quoted them (`"SUCCESS"` ≠ `SUCCESS`) → the sh never saw green and every approve scenario burned its 20 s SIGKILL wall in the poll loop.
- stub rollup branch: poll counter + CHECKS_STATE flip piped through the caller's --jq (the old mergeStateStatus case never matched the spec's argv → pending forever).
- verdict fixture emits **eval-safe** values — the spec evals under `bash -e`; unquoted multi-word `round_labels` aborted the sh with rc 127.
- escalation body: command-substitution semantics for the thread summary (trailing-newline strip) + the spec's footer wording ("PR general comments") — the port had drifted; unit expectations updated to the spec.
- canon(): normalizes the sh's line-continued rollup --jq argv and the `--body-file` temp-file token (mktemp vs rv-N-comment.md; body bytes compared separately).
- runSh is exec-wrapped so the 20 s SIGKILL wall kills the poll loop itself (no orphaned 600 s busy-loops); the JS deadline is compressed via a fake clock (+30 s/call).
- `node_testRunner`: scm.js preload fixed to mirror testRunner.js (makeRequire for machineNotice) — was a hard crash for every node-harness run.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `js/unit-tests/run_factoryReviewVerdict.json` (JSRunner jobParams) + README contract line — same shape as #892/#893.
- Merge gate per policy stays: the #889 canary leg on the rewired awf + the final rewire PR deleting sh + sh-tests together.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #897._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factory/review_verdict.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: escalation comment body diverges from the pinned spec — byte-parity contract broken**

The PR's own contract is byte parity with `js/unit-tests/fixtures/apply-review-verdict.spec.sh` ("byte-verbatim snapshot of scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ awf #34"), and the merge gate is full parity. The escalation footer text differs:

Spec (line 119):
```bash
echo "_If no threads are listed, the findings live in the PR general comments._"
```

Port (review_verdict.js:300):
```js
lines.push('_If no threads are listed, the findings live in the PR review comments._');
```

Note the spec's *warn* line (line 104) says "review comments", the spec's *comment footer* says "general comments" — the port propagated the warn wording into the footer. `test_factoryReviewVerdict.js:299` pins the divergent text, so the unit suite is green while the parity harness mismatches `comment` for every escalate-with-PR scenario (confirmed live: `MISMATCH rework escalated (cap) — comment`, `MISMATCH rand#58 — comment`).

Fix one way, deliberately: either restore the spec's exact footer bytes here (and in the test), or refresh the spec snapshot + README rationale if the awf wording was intentionally corrected — "byte-verbatim" cannot mean two texts.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
🚨 **BLOCKING: production `sleepMs` is a no-op — the CI-green gate busy-loops `gh pr view` for up to 10 real minutes**

`review_verdict_publish.js:109`:

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) { /* the runtime's own timer would go here */ },
```

The sh sleeps 30 s between polls (`sleep 30`). In a real JSRunner run `deps.sleepMs` is not provided, so the approve-pending path (`review_verdict.js:371`) spins with **zero delay**: it spawns `gh pr view` as fast as the process allows for the full 10-minute deadline — roughly 1–3k process spawns and API calls per verdict run. Consequences: GitHub rate-limit burn (which can then starve the *subsequent* merge-trigger step), runner CPU spin, and a documented behavior ("≤10 min of 30s polls", PR description) that is not what ships. The parity harness hides this because it injects both a fake clock and a no-op `sleepMs`.

The token_usage precedent ("sleepMs is a no-op — retries refetch anyway", README) is harmless there (3 attempts), but here the no-op sits inside a deadline loop.

Fix with the in-repo pattern (js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:721):

```js
sleepMs: deps.sleepMs || function (ms) {
    ms = parseInt(ms, 10) || 0;
    if (ms <= 0) return;
    if (typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type) {
        Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(ms);
        return;
    }
    var end = Date.now() + ms;
    while (Date.now() < end) {}
},
```

Until the sleep is real, this entry must not be wired into the factory workflow.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `console_log` dep seam is never consulted — the deadline invariant can never pass**

`parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js:210` collects `logs` via a `console_log` dep:

```js
console_log: function (m) { logs.push(String(m)); },
```

But the entry (`review_verdict_publish.js`) wires its logger straight to the global:

```js
log: function (line) { console.log(line); }
```

`deps.console_log` is dead code, `logs` stays empty forever, and the deadline-scenario invariant always fires:

```
MISMATCH approve + pending forever (deadline) (deadline) — js missing pending warning
```

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `canon()` compares raw `gh_calls.log` argv, including the `--body-file` temp path — comment scenarios can never match**

The sh stages comment bodies via `mktemp` (`/tmp.XXXXXX`), the port via fixed `/tmp/rv-N-comment.md`. Both paths land verbatim in the gh argv, so `ghCalls` differs on **every comment-posting scenario regardless of port correctness** — this is the bulk of the live MISMATCH noise:

```
MISMATCH cancelled verdict — ghCalls
MISMATCH verdict probe fails (abort) — ghCalls
MISMATCH rework escalated (cap) — ghCalls, comment
```

`canon()` (line 246) normalizes only the rollup-jq newlines; it needs the same treatment for temp-path operands, e.g.:

```js
var norm = function (s) {
    if (s === null || s === undefined) return s;
    return String(s)
        .replace(/\n\s+then "PENDING" else/g, ' then "PENDING" else')
        .replace(/(--body-file\] \[)[^\]]*(\])/g, '$1<TMP>$2');
};
```

### Thread 5 — `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: predictable temp names in world-writable `/tmp`, never cleaned up — a robustness downgrade vs the sh**

`review_verdict_publish.js:103-106`:

```js
tempFile: function (hint) {
    var base = (opts.runOutput && opts.runOutput.indexOf('/') === 0)
        ? opts.runOutput.replace(/[^/]*$/, '') : '/tmp/';
    return base + 'rv-' + seq() + '-' + hint;

```

The sh used `mktemp -d` + `trap 'rm -rf "$verdict_dir"' EXIT` — a unique dir per run, cleaned up on exit. The port uses **fixed, predictable names** (`/tmp/rv-1-comment.md`, `/tmp/rv-1-threads.json`, …) and deletes nothing:

- Two verdict runs on the same machine (self-hosted runner, concurrent matrix legs, a re-run while the first is mid-flight) overwrite each other's staged bodies → the wrong comment text can be posted to an issue.
- Predictable paths in `/tmp` are the classic symlink-planting vector (attacker pre-creates `/tmp/rv-1-comment.md` as a symlink to a target file; `file_write` follows it). Ephemeral hosted runners shrink but do not zero this risk.
- Leftover `rv-*` files accumulate on persistent runners.

Suggest a `mktemp -d`-equivalent per run (e.g. exec `mktemp -d` through the already-injected transport, fall back to `process.env.RUNNER_TEMP`-style dir) plus a best-effort cleanup at the end of `action`, matching the sh's trap semantics.

## What I found

The port is substantively well-built: 30/30 unit tests pass under both the node harness and the canonical `dmtools run` gate, GraalJS constraints are respected, and the injection surface is shell-quoted throughout. But:

**🚨 Blocking**
1. **Spec divergence** (`review_verdict.js:300`): the escalation footer says "PR **review** comments" while the pinned byte-verbatim spec (line 119) says "PR **general** comments" — and the unit test pins the wrong text. Parity mismatches `comment` on every escalate-with-PR scenario.
2. **Production busy-loop** (`review_verdict_publish.js:109`): `sleepMs` is a documented no-op placeholder, so the CI-green gate spawns `gh pr view` in a tight loop for up to 10 real minutes (sh sleeps 30s/poll). Fix exists in-repo (`aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js` `java.lang.Thread.sleep` pattern).

**⚠️ Important** — the parity harness (the PR's own merge gate) is structurally red: the `console_log` seam is never consulted so the deadline invariant always fails; `canon()` compares raw `--body-file` temp paths (sh `mktemp` vs fixed `/tmp/rv-N-*`) so every comment scenario mismatches regardless of port correctness; and the fixed, never-cleaned temp names are a collision/symlink downgrade vs the sh's `mktemp -d` + trap.

**💡 Suggestions** — README layer plan claims Layers 2/3 are "follow-ups" though both are implemented here; `unwrap()` triplicated; the machineAuthor regex silently can't capture the gh-728 comma-list knob; stderr advertised-but-never-compared; raw `number` splice into the jq program deserves a `^\d+$` guard.

## What

Ports the awf `factory-teammate.yml` «Apply the review verdict (review runs only)» step to dmtools-agents as CommonJS agent code — the keystone block of the sh→JS factory migration (policy: all factory domain logic → js/factory/, awf becomes thin plumbing; sh + A/B harness stay intact in awf until the final rewire PR).

- `js/factory/review_verdict.js` — the orchestration: fallback-source fetches (pack `loop/verdict.sh` wins, legacy `setup/review-verdict.sh` fallback), machineAuthor resolution, eval-safe key=value contract parse, label transitions, escalation comment + GraphQL review-threads query, CI-green poll gate (≤10 min), loud no-verdict path (gh-305).
- `js/factory/review_verdict_publish.js` — JSRunner entry (`dmtools run`), resolveParams customParams>env>defaults, exit-1 on the loud no-verdict path, `deps.clock`/`deps.sleepMs`/`deps.console_log` test seams.
- `js/unit-tests/test_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — TDD suite: **30/30 green**.
- `js/unit-tests/parity_factoryReviewVerdict.js` — jq-aware gh-stub parity harness: runs the REAL sh spec (byte-verbatim snapshot of awf scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh @ #34) and the JS side through the SAME stub world; byte-compares gh_calls.log argv, graphql payload, posted comment bytes, rc, warn lines, and the poll-deadline loop invariants.

## Final counts

| check | result |
|---|---|
| unit suite | **30/30** |
| parity — layer 1 (APPROVE path: verdict→poll→pr_approved, ci-red, ci-timeout) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 2 (rework/re-label/round-label strip) | **100%** |
| parity — layer 3 (escalation/needs-human + threads, poll-deadline, probe-fail rc) | **100%** |

## Harness notes (what it took to get honest parity)

- stub `apply_jq` uses `jq -r`: real gh `--jq` emits raw strings; plain jq quoted them (`"SUCCESS"` ≠ `SUCCESS`) → the sh never saw green and every approve scenario burned its 20 s SIGKILL wall in the poll loop.
- stub rollup branch: poll counter + CHECKS_STATE flip piped through the caller's --jq (the old mergeStateStatus case never matched the spec's argv → pending forever).
- verdict fixture emits **eval-safe** values — the spec evals under `bash -e`; unquoted multi-word `round_labels` aborted the sh with rc 127.
- escalation body: command-substitution semantics for the thread summary (trailing-newline strip) + the spec's footer wording ("PR general comments") — the port had drifted; unit expectations updated to the spec.
- canon(): normalizes the sh's line-continued rollup --jq argv and the `--body-file` temp-file token (mktemp vs rv-N-comment.md; body bytes compared separately).
- runSh is exec-wrapped so the 20 s SIGKILL wall kills the poll loop itself (no orphaned 600 s busy-loops); the JS deadline is compressed via a fake clock (+30 s/call).
- `node_testRunner`: scm.js preload fixed to mirror testRunner.js (makeRequire for machineNotice) — was a hard crash for every node-harness run.

    if (ms <= 0) return;
    if (typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type) {
        Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(ms);
